articles.title: How Australia played the first music on a computer
articles.summary: Australia played the world's first music on a computer in 1950 or 1951, using a primitive machine called CSIRAC, which was built at the CSIR's radiophysics division in Sydney. The machine was a serial computer, passing digital bits around one at a time, and used mercury acoustic delay lines to store and recall data. Despite its limitations, CSIRAC performed groundbreaking work, including finding the centre of the galaxy in 1953, and was used to engineer the first skyscraper building. The machine's programming involved sending raw pulses from the computer data bus to the speaker, resulting in the unique sound of blurted music.
